label: Title claim
summary: The game concept Title Claim: a legal right to own a title.
details: `[claim|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. A claim gives a casus belli to take the title by war and a valid reason to revoke titles from vassals. Rulers usually get claims on titles they lose, the fabricate claim task can make new ones, and a ruler's children have implicit claims on their titles.

label: Title claim (icon)

label: Claimant

details: `[claimant|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. Ruler claimants can press their claims with the claim casus belli, which can also press the claims of vassals and unlanded characters of the realm. Claimants can lead factions even from outside the realm. Vanilla uses it in decision and faction texts.

label: Claimant faction
summary: The game concept Claimant Faction: a faction that wants to put its claimant on the throne of a title their liege holds.
details: `[claimant_faction|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation. If it wins, the liege gives up the title to the claimant, the vassal structure is rearranged, and all members gain a hook on the claimant. Vanilla uses it in important action and decision texts.

label: Claimant faction
summary: The game concept Claimant Faction: a faction that wants to put its claimant on the throne of a title their liege holds.
details: `[claimant_factions|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in legacy and language concept texts that make vassals less likely to join them.

label: Claimant's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Claimant, a person with claims on titles.
details: `[claimant_possessive|E]` in a text shows the possessive word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in faction texts about a claimant's appeal to vassal stances.

label: Claimant
summary: The game concept Claimant: a person with one or more claims on titles.
details: `[claimants|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the decision that invites claimants to court.

label: Title claim
summary: The game concept Title Claim, shown as the word "Claimed".
details: `[claimed|E]` in a text shows the word linked to the concept's explanation, which describes a claim as a legal right to own a title. Vanilla uses it in an opinion modifier name and a war text about claimed titles.

details: `[claims|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in decision and concept texts, such as which claims can be inherited.

label: Clan house head

details: `[clan_house_heads|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. They get no weak hook on all house members and can be challenged by any house member. Vanilla uses it in the house head concept text, noting they have special rules.

label: Clan (icon)
summary: The icon of the game concept Clan, the government form where vassals' dues depend on the liege's tax collector.
details: `[clan_i|E]` in a text shows the clan government icon linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla puts it in front of the word in clan opinion modifier names.

details: `[clans|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in authority and tutorial texts about house unity.

summary: The game concept Clerical Region Capital: the county a clerical region was founded on, the fixed seat of its clerical title.
details: `[clerical_region_capitals|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Clerical region
summary: The game concept Clerical Region: a geographical region under a clerical title, whose clergy are subordinates of that title's holder.
details: `[clerical_regions|E]` in a text shows the plural word linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in an interaction trigger and as a header in the faith window.

details: `[cloistered_emperor_possessive|E]` in a text shows the possessive word linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this form.

label: Close family

label: Congenital trait
summary: Another name of the game concept Congenital (inheritable traits), shown as the words Congenital Trait.
details: `[congenital_trait|E]` in a text shows Congenital Trait, linked to the explanation of congenital traits: traits a child can inherit, and that breeding can strengthen. Vanilla's texts do not use this form.

label: Congenital traits
summary: The plural name of the game concept Congenital: the traits a character can pass on to their children.
details: `[congenital_traits|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the explanation of congenital traits. Vanilla uses it in the inheritable-traits line of an interaction window and in a modifier for the chance to inherit good ones.

label: Conqueror icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Conqueror (the AI personality that wants to grow its realm by war at any cost).
details: `[conqueror_i]` in a text shows the conqueror icon; vanilla writes it right before the word, as in the conqueror game rule and the conqueror AI personality's name. A Conqueror puts its gold into its war chest or into men-at-arms, starts many more wars and is an unreliable ally.

label: Roll of patrons
summary: The game concept Roll of Patrons: an adventurer's list of characters who support them.
details: `[contact_list|E]` in a text shows the words Roll of Patrons, linked to the concept's explanation. The list holds everyone the adventurer finished a task contract for, plus others with a reason to help, such as fond family, friends and lovers. The adventurer can ask these patrons for extra support with a character interaction. Vanilla uses it where a contract or a scheme adds someone to the list.

label: Roll of patrons
summary: Another name of the game concept Roll of Patrons, used for one patron on an adventurer's list.
details: `[contact_list_contact|E]` in a text shows the word for a single patron, linked to the Roll of Patrons explanation (the characters who support an adventurer). Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as every patron with a positive opinion, and in a task contract's requirement.

label: Roll of patrons
summary: Another name of the game concept Roll of Patrons, used for the patrons on an adventurer's list.
details: `[contact_list_contacts|E]` in a text shows the plural word, linked to the Roll of Patrons explanation. Vanilla uses it in texts about a camp's range: moving far puts the adventurer out of reach of their patrons, and provisions can be requested from them.

label: Contest
summary: The game concept Contest: one of the competitions of a tournament, where qualified contestants compete for prizes.
details: `[contest|E]` in a text shows the word Contest, linked to the concept's explanation. The tournament's host chooses the contests. Each one picks its winner in one of four ways: knock-out, turns, teams or race. Skills, traits and preparation decide the chance to win; who may enter physical contests depends on health, sex and the host's culture and faith.

label: Contest aptitude
summary: The game concept Contest Aptitude: how good a character is at a kind of tournament contest (foot, horse, bow, wit, or a mix).
details: `[contest_aptitude|E]` in a text shows the words Contest Aptitude, linked to the concept's explanation. Aptitude comes from skills, health, traits and the experience of the tourney participant trait; a giant with high prowess, for example, does well at wrestling. Vanilla uses it in modifier texts that raise or lower it.

label: Race
summary: The game concept Race: the contest format where the qualified contestant whose horse finishes first wins.
details: `[contest_category_race|E]` in a text shows the word Race, linked to the concept's explanation. The horse race is the contest of this format. Vanilla uses it in the contest format line of tournaments.

label: Teams
summary: The game concept Teams: the contest format where every qualified contestant on the team with the most points at the end gets rewards.
details: `[contest_category_team|E]` in a text shows the word Teams, linked to the concept's explanation. The melee is the contest of this format.

label: Turns
summary: The game concept Turns: the contest format where the qualified contestant with the most points at the end wins.
details: `[contest_category_turn|E]` in a text shows the word Turns, linked to the concept's explanation. Archery and the recital are contests of this format.

label: Knock-out
summary: The game concept Knock-Out: the contest format where qualified contestants face each other in bouts over three rounds until one is left.
details: `[contest_category_versus|E]` in a text shows the word Knock-Out, linked to the concept's explanation. Wrestling, the duel, the joust and board games are contests of this format.

label: Qualification
summary: The game concept Qualification: whether a contestant gets a place in a tournament contest.
details: `[contest_qualification|E]` in a text shows the word Qualification, linked to the concept's explanation. Many characters may be eligible, but only a few qualify for each contest. A character whose progress to victory is above the threshold when the contest starts is sure to qualify. Vanilla uses it in message filters for changes to a character's or their champion's qualification.

label: Qualification
summary: Another name of the game concept Qualification, shown as the word Qualifier.
details: `[contest_qualifier|E]` in a text shows Qualifier, linked to the Qualification explanation (only a few eligible characters get a place in each contest). Vanilla's texts do not use this form.

label: Qualification
summary: Another name of the game concept Qualification, shown as the word Qualifiers.
details: `[contest_qualifiers|E]` in a text shows Qualifiers, linked to the Qualification explanation. Vanilla's texts do not use this form.

label: Qualification
summary: Another name of the game concept Qualification, written as the verb qualifies (a contestant qualifies for a contest).
details: `[contest_qualifies|E]` in a text shows the verb, linked to the Qualification explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in a concept text about gaining prestige when one of the ruler's knights qualifies for or wins a tournament contest.

label: Qualification
summary: Another name of the game concept Qualification, shown as the verb Qualify.
details: `[contest_qualify|E]` in a text shows Qualify, linked to the Qualification explanation: only a few eligible characters get a place in each tournament contest. Vanilla's texts do not use this form.

label: Qualification
summary: Another name of the game concept Qualification, written as qualifying (the contestants who have a place in a contest).
details: `[contest_qualifying|E]` in a text shows the word, linked to the Qualification explanation. Vanilla's concept texts write it before contestants, as in the qualifying contestants of a contest.

label: Contest round
summary: The game concept Contest Round: one of the three rounds of a knock-out contest (quarter-finals, semi-finals and the final).
details: `[contest_round|E]` in a text shows the words Contest Round, linked to the concept's explanation. In knock-out contests the qualified contestants are paired against each other in bouts until only one is left. Vanilla's texts use the plural form instead.

label: Contest round
summary: The plural name of the game concept Contest Round: the rounds of a knock-out contest.
details: `[contest_rounds|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Contest Round explanation (quarter-finals, semi-finals and the final). Vanilla uses it in the knock-out explanation and in a tournament text giving the number of rounds as 3.

label: Contestant
summary: The game concept Contestant: a character who competes in a tournament contest.
details: `[contestant|E]` in a text shows the word Contestant, linked to the concept's explanation. Each contest has requirements: board games are open to all, others such as wrestling depend on martial rules, and the host's culture and religion decide by gender and health who may enter. Those who do not compete are spectators, and a possible contestant may choose to watch instead. Vanilla lines that write `[contestant.GetHerHis]` and similar use a saved character of the same name in memory texts, not this concept.

label: Contestant
summary: The plural name of the game concept Contestant: the characters who compete in a tournament contest.
details: `[contestants|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Contestant explanation. Vanilla uses it in the concept texts about contests and their formats.

label: Contest
summary: The plural name of the game concept Contest: the competitions of a tournament.
details: `[contests|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Contest explanation. Vanilla uses it in building texts about cheaper contests in a holding and in concept texts about tournaments and prizes.

label: Military assistance
summary: The game concept Military Assistance: an interaction that lets rulers involved in the Iberian struggle join each other's wars for gold.
details: `[contract_assistance|E]` in a text shows the words Military Assistance, linked to the concept's explanation. Payment comes when the war ends, whatever the outcome, as long as the helping ruler reached a war contribution of at least 100. Vanilla uses it in the texts telling who paid or did not pay whom for the help.

label: Military assistance
summary: Another name of the game concept Military Assistance, shown as the words Assisting Militarily (giving paid help in another struggle ruler's war).
details: `[contract_assisting|E]` in a text shows Assisting Militarily, linked to the Military Assistance explanation. Vanilla uses it once, in the message that the character is already assisting in a war.

label: Contract scheme
summary: The game concept Contract Scheme: a scheme an adventurer must complete to fulfil a task contract.
details: `[contract_scheme|E]` in a text shows the words Contract Scheme, linked to the concept's explanation. These schemes can be harmful (murdering the contractor's rival), pleasant (entertaining their court with stories) or harmless (copying texts). If the scheme fails or is abandoned, the task contract fails too.

label: Contract scheme
summary: Another name of the game concept Contract Scheme, shown as the word Contract.
details: `[contract_scheme_contract|E]` in a text shows the word Contract, linked to the Contract Scheme explanation (a scheme an adventurer must finish for a task contract). Vanilla uses it once, in the description of a contract scheme.

label: Contract scheme
summary: The possessive name of the game concept Contract Scheme, shown as Contract Scheme's.
details: `[contract_scheme_possessive|E]` in a text shows Contract Scheme's, linked to the explanation of contract schemes. Vanilla's texts do not use this form.

label: Contract scheme
summary: The plural name of the game concept Contract Scheme: schemes adventurers must complete for task contracts.
details: `[contract_schemes|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Contract Scheme explanation. Vanilla's scheme explanation lists them as one of the four kinds of scheme, and the only kind whose success chance can go above 95%.

label: Contract scheme
summary: The plural possessive name of the game concept Contract Scheme, shown as Contract Schemes'.
details: `[contract_schemes_possessive|E]` in a text shows Contract Schemes', linked to the explanation of contract schemes. Vanilla's texts do not use this form.

label: Contractor
summary: The game concept Contractor: the character who puts out a task contract for adventurers.
details: `[contractor|E]` in a text shows the word Contractor, linked to the concept's explanation. The contract mostly concerns the contractor, who usually pays the adventurer. Criminal contracts are the exception: they are usually not put out by the contractor but exploit them, for example by tricking a gullible person out of gold.

label: Contractor
summary: The possessive name of the game concept Contractor (the character who puts out a task contract).
details: `[contractor_possessive|E]` in a text shows the possessive, linked to the Contractor explanation. Vanilla uses it in contract scheme descriptions, such as the contractor's court or the contractor's land.

label: Contractor
summary: The plural name of the game concept Contractor: the characters who put out task contracts.
details: `[contractors|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Contractor explanation. Vanilla uses it in contract scheme descriptions.

label: Contractor
summary: The plural possessive name of the game concept Contractor.
details: `[contractors_possessive|E]` in a text shows the plural possessive, linked to the Contractor explanation (the characters who put out task contracts). Vanilla uses it once, in a contract scheme description about dangerous lands.

label: War contribution
summary: Another name of the game concept War Contribution, shown as the verb Contribute.
details: `[contribute|E]` in a text shows Contribute, linked to the War Contribution explanation: rulers helping allies in a war earn contribution from battles (lost ones too) and occupied holdings, and are rewarded for it when the war ends, usually with gold, prestige or piety. Vanilla's texts do not use this form.

label: War contribution
summary: Another name of the game concept War Contribution: how much a ruler has done to help allies in a war.
details: `[contribution|E]` in a text shows the word, linked to the War Contribution explanation. Contribution grows with the number and size of battles fought, even lost ones, and with occupied holdings; at the end of the war each helper is rewarded by it, depending on the casus belli. Vanilla uses it in interaction texts that pay gold by contribution.

label: County control
summary: Another name of the game concept County Control: how firmly the government holds the people of a county.
details: `[control|E]` in a text shows the word Control, linked to the County Control explanation. Control matters most for taxes from the holdings. It drops sharply when a county is taken in war, and sieges and peasant uprisings damage it; low control can bring county corruption, and the marshal's council task raises it. Vanilla uses it in the texts of control changes.

label: County control icon
summary: The icon of the game concept County Control (how firmly the government holds a county).
details: `[control_i]` in a text shows the control icon; vanilla writes it before a value, as in the control changes by an amount.

label: Convert faith in county
summary: Another name of the game concept Convert Faith in County (the court chaplain's council task), shown as the verb Convert.
details: `[convert|E]` in a text shows Convert, linked to the explanation of the conversion task. Vanilla uses it once, in a law text saying vassals are more inclined to convert to the ruler's faith.

label: Convert faith in county
summary: The game concept Convert Faith in County: the court chaplain's council task that converts a county of another faith or rite.
details: `[convert_county|E]` in a text shows the task's name, linked to the concept's explanation. Progress grows each month; at 100% most of the county takes the chaplain's faith. The rite follows the liege when the new faith is the liege's, otherwise it is the chaplain's own rite. Many things change the speed, such as the councillor's skill.

label: Convert faith in county
summary: Another name of the game concept Convert Faith in County, written as converted (a county the chaplain has converted).
details: `[converted|E]` in a text shows the word, linked to the explanation of the chaplain's conversion task. Vanilla uses it in the message that a councillor has converted a county. The memory line that writes `[converted.GetName]` uses a saved county of the same name, not this concept.

label: Convert faith in county
summary: Another name of the game concept Convert Faith in County, written as converting (the chaplain's conversion task is under way).
details: `[converting|E]` in a text shows the word, linked to the explanation of the conversion task. Vanilla uses it in the messages that a councillor is converting, or has stopped converting, a county.

label: Convince de jure territory
summary: The game concept Convince De Jure Territory: the steward's council task that persuades a county to come back to its rightful liege.
details: `[convince_dejure|E]` in a text shows the task's name, linked to the concept's explanation. It targets a county that rightfully (de jure) belongs to the steward's liege but is owned by an independent ruler. Once persuaded, the county asks its ruler to release it to that liege. Vanilla uses it where a court grandeur level unlocks the task.

label: Tenet
summary: Another name of the game concept Tenet, shown as the word Core (a tenet that is part of a faith).
details: `[core|E]` in a text shows Core, linked to the Tenet explanation: where doctrines are positions a rite must take, tenets are its own customs and practices. Vanilla uses it once, in a decision requiring a tenet to be permitted or core to the faith.

label: Tenet
summary: Another name of the game concept Tenet, shown as the word Tenet: one of a faith's defining customs and practices.
details: `[core_tenet|E]` in a text shows the word Tenet, linked to the Tenet explanation (tenets are a rite's own quirks, beside the doctrines it must take a stance on). Vanilla uses it often, in requirements such as having or not having a given tenet.

label: Core
summary: The game concept Core: the tenet status of a tenet or doctrine that a rite actively promotes as one of its defining practices.
details: `[core_tenet_status|E]` in a text shows the word Core, linked to the concept's explanation. Every follower of the rite is subject to the effects of a core tenet or doctrine. Vanilla uses it next to the permitted status, as in a tenet that is already permitted or core in the faith.

label: Tenet
summary: The plural name of the game concept Tenet, shown as Tenets: a faith's defining customs and practices.
details: `[core_tenets|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Tenet explanation. Vanilla's concept texts use it for the beliefs of a faith's main rite and for what holy orders spread.

label: Coronation
summary: The game concept Coronation: an activity where a ruler invites vassals, peers and guests to witness their ascension to the throne.
details: `[coronation|E]` in a text shows the word Coronation, linked to the concept's explanation. It comes as a regular coronation or as an anointment, which costs more and rewards more. Vanilla's texts say kings and emperors who have not held one are seen as illegitimate by their vassals.

label: Anointment
summary: The game concept Anointment: the kind of coronation where the ruler seeks the blessing of their head of faith (or the head of their rite when there is none).
details: `[coronation_anointment|E]` in a text shows the word Anointment, linked to the concept's explanation. In some faiths it is needed to count as a truly legitimate ruler. The host can win the religious authority's support with the anointment request interaction. Vanilla uses it in coronation activity texts about who has access to the anointment option.

label: Detractor
summary: The game concept Detractor: a guest at a coronation who opposes the host's ascension and tries to ruin their legitimacy.
details: `[coronation_detractor|E]` in a text shows the word Detractor, linked to the concept's explanation. Detractors stand against the coronation's supporters. Vanilla uses it in faction reasons and in coronation intent texts.

label: Detractor
summary: The plural name of the game concept Detractor: the coronation guests who work against the host.
details: `[coronation_detractors|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Detractor explanation. Vanilla uses it in coronation texts, such as an intent that harms detractors and the window of the detractors with the biggest impact.

label: Coronation icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Coronation (the activity where a ruler is crowned before guests).
details: `[coronation_i]` in a text shows the coronation activity icon; vanilla writes it before the word, as in `[coronation_i][coronation|E]`, and before coronation oath labels.

label: Magnificence
summary: The game concept Magnificence: the score of a coronation that decides how well it turns out for the host.
details: `[coronation_magnificence|E]` in a text shows the word Magnificence, linked to the concept's explanation. A higher score gives the host a better outcome. Intents, activity options and the activity's events raise it, and supporters and detractors can change it too.

label: Supporter
summary: The game concept Supporter: a guest at a coronation who backs the host's ascension and can help secure their legitimacy.
details: `[coronation_supporter|E]` in a text shows the word Supporter, linked to the concept's explanation. Supporters stand against the coronation's detractors. Vanilla uses it in coronation texts, such as vassals who swore loyalty as supporters.

label: Supporter
summary: The plural name of the game concept Supporter: the coronation guests who back the host.
details: `[coronation_supporters|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Supporter explanation. Vanilla uses it in intent texts that please supporters and in texts about problems for the host and their supporters.

label: Coronation
summary: The plural name of the game concept Coronation: the activities where rulers are crowned.
details: `[coronations|E]` in a text shows the plural, linked to the Coronation explanation. Vanilla uses it in a game rule text saying the AI holds coronations less often.

label: Council
summary: The game concept Council: the six councillors who help a ruler run the realm.
details: `[council|E]` in a text shows the word Council, linked to the concept's explanation. Each councillor heads a department and can be given council tasks. Vanilla uses it in texts about leaving or being fired from a council.

label: Council icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Council (the ruler's six councillors).
details: `[council_i]` in a text shows the council icon; vanilla writes it before a scheme agent offer of a guaranteed council seat.

label: Councillor
summary: The game concept Councillor: one of a ruler's main helpers on the council.
details: `[councillor|E]` in a text shows the word Councillor, linked to the concept's explanation. The six seats are chancellor, marshal, steward, spymaster, court chaplain (or realm priest) and the spouse; each runs a department with its own tasks. Powerful vassals are upset when they get no seat.

label: Councillor task
summary: The game concept Councillor Task: a job a ruler gives one of their councillors.
details: `[councillor_task|E]` in a text shows the words, linked to the concept's explanation. A task can be general or aimed at a county or a court. A relation with the councillor can make tasks with a completion time take longer or shorter. Councillors only lead the effort; they do not travel to do it.
